title: Father Brian Junkes returns to Royal Palm Beach for Masses of thanksgiving
text:
Father Brian Junkes returns to Royal Palm Beach for Masses of thanksgiving
Newly ordained Father Brian Junkes returned to Our Lady Queen of the Apostles Church in Royal Palm Beach on May 30 and 31, where he celebrated Masses of thanksgiving with friends and family, including his parents, Harald and Ann Junkes. After being ordained as a priest of the Society of the Divine Word on May 23 in Chicago, Father Junkes came back to the Diocese of Palm Beach to honor his beginnings.
Born in Coral Springs and raised in The Acreage west of West Palm Beach since 1990, Father Junkes recalled attending religious education classes and Mass at Our Lady Queen of the Apostles. He said it was during a confirmation retreat that he first had a faith-affirming experience. “That was the first time I really felt, ‘Wow, God’s real. God exists.’ I had a very powerful experience,” Father Junkes said. “And so then, when I finished confirmation, I went straight to being in the youth group, or back then it was called the LifeTeen group.”
During high school, he participated in parish youth activities and helped with confirmation classes. He began considering priesthood after attending Vocation Awareness Week at St. John Vianney College Seminary but followed his mother’s advice to work and attend college before making any decisions about entering seminary. “My last year of high school, I got a job working at Pinch-a-Penny selling swimming pool supplies and was there for five and a half years,” Father Junkes said. “Worked my way up to being a supervisor, and then I did go to Palm Beach State College for three semesters.”
He described praying for guidance until receiving what he considered a sign during a pilgrimage to Poland in May 2012 with his pastor from OLQA: sitting unknowingly where Pope John Paul II used to pray at Krakow’s Church of St. Mary. After visiting Divine Word College Seminary later that year in Iowa, he entered formation with the Society of the Divine Word.
As part of his training with the order known for its international character, Father Junkes studied Spanish in Mexico before spending nearly two years serving parishes in Chad through their Cross-Cultural Training Program: “Normally it’s a year... they encourage us to go to a culture different from our own... So I went to Chad in Africa,” he said.
Currently assigned within the U.S. Southern Province stretching from Texas to Florida while completing an MA degree program at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago, Father Junkes reflected on those who influenced him at OLQA: priests from various countries who taught him about living out faith locally as well as abroad. "With mission," Father Junkes said, "it doesn’t necessarily mean you have to go to another country like I did... Right in our own communities—that’s mission—and that mission is instilled in us by God."
